positions.as_written: Avoid citing a dissection study to settle a clinical question.
Measure slope before choosing between augmentation and correction.
Consider both in the knee that has failed a conventional revision.
State that no trial compares them directly.
Set the question out as a balance and name what sits on each side of it.
Weigh age and pivoting demand first, because the benefit concentrates there.
Measure slope before treating augmentation as the only available lever.
Price a second failure into the revision decision rather than into the primary one.

Take age and physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and the patient's own ideas, concerns and expectations into the decision explicitly, because a trial population carries none of them.
Accept that the same evidence can be weighed differently without either consultant being wrong.
Follow registry and subgroup data as it accumulates.
